chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who says to another man, 'Buy goods for me, and the profit is shared between me and you,' so he said, 'There is no harm (in it).'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to share profits in a trade partnership where one party buys goods for the other?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates a specific trade partnership (*Mudarabah*-like structure) where one party instructs the purchase of goods and profits are shared, ruling it as permissible (*la ba'sa*). This ruling is significant in Shia commercial jurisprudence as it distinguishes this instructional partnership from prohibited elements of uncertainty (*gharar*) or interest (*riba*), provided the terms are clear. It underscores the flexibility of Islamic contract law in facilitating trade while maintaining ethical boundaries.
